knowledge:
- key_parameters: on_disk=Logical indicating whether to store images on disk as HDF5 files (TRUE) or in memory (FALSE) ;; h5FilesPath=Character path specifying where to write HDF5 files when on_disk is TRUE ;; colour_by=Character vector of channel names or metadata columns to color the images or cells (supports up to 6 channels) ;; outline_by=Character specifying the metadata column in the SingleCellExperiment to outline cells by ;; img_id=Character indicating the colData and elementMetadata entry containing matching image identifiers ;; cell_id=Character indicating the colData entry containing cell identifiers matching pixel values in segmentation masks ;; exprs_values=Character specifying which assay slot in the SingleCellExperiment to use for cell-level expression (e.g., "counts", "exprs") ;; bcg=Named list of channel-specific brightness, contrast, and gamma adjustments (each as a numeric vector of length 3) ;; return_plot=Logical indicating whether to return the recorded plot object ;; return_images=Logical indicating whether to return a SimpleList of three-color Image objects
- alternatives: In-memory storage (on_disk = FALSE, default) is recommended for small image sets because it is faster and more efficient. On-disk storage (on_disk = TRUE) is preferred for large image sets (hundreds to thousands of images) to avoid running out of memory.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing highly multiplexed imaging cytometry data where pixel-level intensities, segmentation masks, and cell-level expression/metadata need to be integrated, measured, and visualized.
- pitfalls: CellProfiler-processed images are scaled between 0 and 1 by default; segmentation masks must be scaled back (e.g., multiplied by 2^16 - 1) to restore integer cell IDs. When using on_disk = TRUE, the normalize function writes a second dataset to the same HDF5 file (increasing disk size unless overwrite = TRUE, which breaks existing R links). setChannels stores replacement values in memory, increasing memory usage even when on disk. mergeChannels creates a new file and requires a new h5FilesPath. img_id and cell_id must match exactly between the SingleCellExperiment and CytoImageList objects. Channel names do not support duplicated entries.

workflows.name: pixel_and_cell_visualization
workflows.intent: Load, scale, measure, and visualize pixel-level intensities and cell-level expression/metadata from multiplexed images and segmentation masks in memory.
input: multi_channel_images.tiff (multi-channel tiff stack of pixel intensities)
segmentation_masks.tiff (single-channel tiff of cell segmentation masks)
workflows.stages:
1. Load segmentation masks and multi-channel images using loadImages.
2. Add image metadata to the elementMetadata slot of both CytoImageList objects.
3. Scale segmentation masks using scaleImages to restore integer cell IDs.
4. Set channel names using channelNames.
5. Measure cell-specific intensities and morphological features to generate a SingleCellExperiment using measureObjects.
6. Plot pixel-level intensities using plotPixels.
7. Plot cell-level expression and metadata on segmentation masks using plotCells.
workflows.code:
path.to.images <- system.file("extdata", package = "cytomapper")
all_masks <- loadImages(path.to.images, pattern = "_mask.tiff")
all_stacks <- loadImages(path.to.images, pattern = "_imc.tiff")
mcols(all_masks)$ImageNb <- c("1", "2", "3")
mcols(all_stacks)$ImageNb <- c("1", "2", "3")
all_masks <- scaleImages(all_masks, 2^16-1)
channelNames(all_stacks) <- c("H3", "CD99", "PIN", "CD8a", "CDH")
sce <- measureObjects(all_masks, all_stacks, img_id = "ImageNb")
data(pancreasSCE)
data(pancreasImages)
data(pancreasMasks)
plotPixels(image = pancreasImages, colour_by = c("H3", "CD99", "CDH"))
plotCells(mask = pancreasMasks, object = pancreasSCE, cell_id = "CellNb", img_id = "ImageNb", colour_by = "CD99", outline_by = "CellType")
plotCells(mask = pancreasMasks, object = pancreasSCE, cell_id = "CellNb", img_id = "ImageNb", colour_by = "CellType")

workflows.name: on_disk_image_handling
workflows.intent: Load and process large sets of images on disk using HDF5 format to minimize memory usage.
input: large_segmentation_masks.tiff (large single-channel tiff of cell segmentation masks)
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize a temporary or permanent directory for HDF5 files using getHDF5DumpDir.
2. Load images directly to disk using loadImages with on_disk = TRUE and h5FilesPath.
3. Scale on-disk images using scaleImages.
4. Convert existing in-memory CytoImageList objects to on-disk representation using CytoImageList.
5. Convert on-disk CytoImageList objects back to in-memory representation if needed.
6. Normalize on-disk images using normalize.
7. Merge channels on-disk using mergeChannels.
workflows.code:
library(HDF5Array)
cur_dir <- getHDF5DumpDir()
path.to.images <- system.file("extdata", package = "cytomapper")
image.list <- loadImages(path.to.images, pattern = "mask.tiff", on_disk = TRUE, h5FilesPath = cur_dir)
image.list <- scaleImages(image.list, value = 2^16 - 1)
data("pancreasImages")
pancreasImages_onDisk <- CytoImageList(pancreasImages, on_disk = TRUE, h5FilesPath = cur_dir)
pancreasImages_inMemory <- CytoImageList(pancreasImages_onDisk, on_disk = FALSE)
pancreasImages_norm <- normalize(pancreasImages_onDisk)
channels1 <- getChannels(pancreasImages_onDisk, 1:2)
channels2 <- getChannels(pancreasImages_onDisk, 3:4)
dir.create(file.path(cur_dir, "test"))
cur_path_2 <- file.path(cur_dir, "test")
channels3 <- mergeChannels(channels1, channels2, h5FilesPath = cur_path_2)
